question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14118773/assets/9773630254747a4bbd072bd44a6263bdd078fa09005b1bb5f51c48b894d67daf.svg)

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -12 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14118773/assets/43b9b089e0f93e63acf386bb605a0e3751cc8660899ce19d23835f9f79918bcc.svg)

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x - 3y = 1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=1+3y,$ and the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14118773/assets/4a598a80f2f14715d1f10d182b3f80887c7586beabecc2a329119b624c19a4fa.svg)

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1+3y \\ y\end{aligned}]=⟨1+3y,\,y⟩,\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
